The lounge host flagged a thought on bedding supplies after a rushed handover. Incident Report - Bedding Mix-Up and Pet Comfort Check

The issue started at the gate side lounge when a traveler arrived with a carrier and the pet relief kit did not match the handover notes. The bedding in the carrier looked thin and damp, and the traveler said the swap had happened during a quick transition between ground staff. The cabin team was alerted before boarding, and the companion animal was moved to a quieter spot so the bag could be opened and checked without adding stress. I noted the mismatch in the service record and confirmed the traveler had been given the wrong pack for the flight segment. The traveler became upset over the condition of the bedding and said the pet had already been unsettled by the delay. <<FACT F113>> The lounge host then pointed out that a spare liner had been kept aside for backup use, which helped calm the situation enough to continue.

The handling steps were taken in order. Fresh bedding was brought from the secure stock, the carrier was cleaned, and the pet was checked by the cabin lead before boarding. The crew received a direct reminder to watch for any sign of overheating or distress once the animal was seated. <<FACT F117>> The traveler was told to speak up right away if the pet showed heavy breathing, agitation, or any wetness in the carrier. The note was also passed to the ground desk so the next handover would be checked more carefully and the supply bag would be sealed and labeled before release.

Follow-up is still active. The supervisor asked for a review of the handover chain, the bedding stock count, and the lounge handoff habits that let the mix-up happen. The traveler left with the corrected kit, and the pet settled once the new liner was in place. Companion Animal Travel Desk
